headings: Natural Gas NGLs and Oil Total
paragraphs: We are a vertically integrated natural gas company with upstream, gathering and transmission operations focused in the Appalachian Basin. As of December 31, 2025, we had 28.0 Tcfe of proved natural gas, NGLs and oil reserves across approximately 2.3 million gross acres and approximately 2,945 miles of pipeline infrastructure. In addition, we own an investment in Series A of Mountain Valley Pipeline, LLC (MVP A), which owns the Mountain Valley Pipeline (MVP Mainline), a 303-mile-long pipeline that spans from Wetzel County, West Virginia to Pittsylvania County, Virginia.

Our core business strategy is to be the leading low-cost producer of natural gas with a business model designed to generate durable free cash flow across commodity price cycles. This strategy relies on our substantial inventory of core drilling locations, our vast midstream infrastructure spanning across the Appalachian Basin, our investment grade credit metrics, the low emissions profile of our operations and our best-in-class team and culture. As the only large-scale, integrated natural gas producer in the United States, we believe we are well positioned to excel during times of market volatility and to serve growing sources of demand, including power generation, industrial consumption, domestic data center development and LNG exports.

Our operational strategy centers on the execution of large-scale, multi-pad development projects, which we refer to as combo-development. Combo-development generates value across all levels of the reserves development process by maximizing operational and capital efficiencies. In the drilling stage, rigs spend more time drilling and less time transitioning to new sites. Advanced planning, a prerequisite to pursuing combo-development, facilitates the delivery of bulk hydraulic fracturing sand and piped fresh and recycled water and provides the ability to continuously meet completions supply needs and the use of environmentally friendly technologies such as electric hydraulic fracturing powered by natural gas. Our operational strategy is further enhanced by our robust midstream pipelines and services, which are synchronized with the timing of our development plan. Our synchronized development plan supports an integrated business model that keeps development costs low and limits our need to hedge future production.

Combo-development also provides meaningful environmental and social benefits when compared to more fragmented development approaches. Our operational strategy is integrated with our sustainability framework, which emphasizes continuous improvement in emissions performance, data quality and transparency, workforce development and stakeholder engagement. By concentrating development activity, combo-development results in fewer well sites, reduced truck traffic, lower fuel consumption, shorter and fewer periods of surface disturbance and reduced incremental midstream construction, contributing to improved safety performance and reduced environmental and community impacts.

Further, our integrated business model provides resilience across pricing environments. In periods of low commodity prices, our midstream assets support durable free cash flow due to their annuity-like nature of generating stable, predictable, long-term revenue. In periods of high commodity prices, our low-cost structure permits lower levels of financial hedging, thus providing increased exposure to higher natural gas prices. Correspondingly, we have implemented a robust capital allocation strategy directed at responsibly developing our assets and positioning us for organic growth, while also returning capital to our shareholders through a combination of debt retirements, a base dividend and opportunistic share repurchases. We are also focused on maintaining and strengthening our investment grade credit metrics, which improve our access to reliable, low-cost capital throughout market cycles.

We believe the benefits of our operating model can be enhanced through select strategic transactions, and, as such, part of our strategy also includes creating value through mergers and acquisitions, divestitures, joint ventures and similar business transactions as well as investing in energy-related opportunities directed at complementing and, in certain cases, diversifying our core business operations.

Our proprietary digital work environment, the size and contiguity of our asset base, and our robust midstream pipeline network uniquely position us to execute on a multi-decade inventory of combo-development projects in our core acreage position. Through disciplined execution of our strategy, we aim to be the operator of choice for our stakeholders while supporting the reliable supply of natural gas to meet domestic needs and growing global demand, in a manner that promotes energy security, affordability and sustainable development.
•Achieved sales volume of 2,382 Bcfe, with an average realized price of $3.19 per Mcfe.
•Generated $5.1 billion of net cash provided by operating activities.
•Delivered on our shareholder return strategy through debt retirements and dividends.
◦Retired $1.4 billion aggregate principal of senior notes.
◦Paid $390 million aggregate dividends to shareholders.
◦Increased the quarterly base dividend by 5% to $0.165 per share ($0.66 per share annualized).
•Increased total proved reserves by 1,782 Bcfe, or 7%, compared to 2024.

headings: Risks Associated with Natural Gas Upstream, Midstream and Processing Operations
We are subject to risks associated with the operation of our wells, pipelines and facilities.
A terrorist attack or armed conflict targeting our systems or natural gas infrastructure generally could materially adversely impact our operations.
Our drilling locations are scheduled out over many years, making them susceptible to uncertainties that could materially alter the occurrence or timing of when they are drilled, if at all.
Failure to timely develop our leased real property could result in increased capital expenditures and/or impairment of our leases.
We do not own all of the land on which our pipelines and facilities are located, which could disrupt our operations and future development.
We may incur losses as a result of title defects in the properties we lease.
The amount and timing of actual future natural gas, NGLs and oil production is difficult to predict and may vary significantly from our estimates, which may reduce our earnings.
The standardized measure of discounted future net cash flows from our proved reserves is not the same as the current market value of our estimated natural gas, NGLs and oil reserves.
Financial and Market Risks Applicable to Our Business

We may not be able to increase our customer throughput and resulting revenue due to competition and other factors, which could limit our ability to grow our Gathering segment and Transmission segment.
A financial crisis or deterioration in general economic, business or geopolitical conditions could materially adversely affect our operations and financial condition.
paragraphs: In addition to the other information contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, the following risk factors make an investment in us speculative or risky and should be considered in evaluating our business and future prospects. Note that additional risks not presently known to us or that are currently considered immaterial may also have a negative impact on our business and operations. If any of the events or circumstances described below actually occur, our business, financial condition or results of operations could suffer and the trading price of EQT common stock or other securities could decline.

Drilling for, producing, gathering, transmitting, storing and processing natural gas are high-risk and costly activities with many uncertainties. Our future financial position, cash flows and results of operations depend on the success of our operating activities, which are subject to numerous risks beyond our control.

Many factors may curtail, delay, suspend or cancel our scheduled drilling projects, the development schedule of wells which we do not operate but in which we have a working interest (referred to as non-operated wells), and our gathering, transmission, storage and processing operations, including the following:

•delays imposed by or resulting from compliance with regulatory requirements, including limitations resulting from permitting, wastewater disposal, emission of GHGs, and limitations on hydraulic fracturing;
•shortages of or delays in obtaining equipment, rigs, pipe, materials, qualified personnel, water (for hydraulic fracturing activities) or other natural resources needed for our operations;
•supply chain disruptions or labor shortage impacts; •equipment failures, accidents or other unexpected operational events;

The following discussion and analysis of financial condition and results of operations should be read in conjunction with the Consolidated Financial Statements and the notes thereto included in Item 8., "Financial Statements and Supplementary Data."

Our results of operation for 2025 reflect our acquisition (the Olympus Energy Acquisition) of certain oil and gas properties and related upstream and midstream assets from Olympus Energy LLC, Hyperion Midstream LLC and Bow & Arrow Land Company LLC (collectively, Olympus Energy), which was completed on July 1, 2025. See Note 11 to the Consolidated Financial Statements for further discussion of the Olympus Energy Acquisition.

Our results of operation for 2025 reflect the impact of the Midstream Joint Venture Transaction (defined in Note 9 to the Consolidated Financial Statements), where we received $3.5 billion of cash consideration from a third-party investor in exchange for a noncontrolling equity interest in the Midstream Joint Venture. The Midstream Joint Venture Transaction was completed on December 30, 2024.
NEPA Non-Operated Asset Divestitures and NEPA Gathering System Acquisition

Beginning May 31, 2024, our results of operations reflect (i) our divestiture (the First NEPA Non-Operated Asset Divestiture) of an undivided 40% interest in our non-operated natural gas assets in Northeast Pennsylvania and (ii) our 100% ownership of the NEPA Gathering System (defined in Note 11 to the Consolidated Financial Statements) following our acquisition of additional ownership interests therein in connection with the NEPA Gathering System Acquisition (defined in Note 11 to the Consolidated Financial Statements) and the First NEPA Non-Operated Asset Divestiture.

In addition, our results of operations for 2025 reflect our divestiture (the Second NEPA Non-Operated Asset Divestiture, and together with the First NEPA Non-Operated Asset Divestiture, the NEPA Non-Operated Asset Divestitures) of the remaining undivided 60% interest in our non-operated natural gas assets in Northeast Pennsylvania, which was completed on December 31, 2024. See Note 12 to the Consolidated Financial Statements for further discussion of the NEPA Non-Operated Asset Divestitures.
Beginning July 22, 2024, our results of operations reflect our operation of the assets acquired in the Equitrans Midstream Merger (defined in Note 11 to the Consolidated Financial Statements).

Following the Equitrans Midstream Merger, the gathering and transmission services previously provided to us by Equitrans Midstream are provided to our Upstream segment by our Gathering and Transmission segments as affiliate transactions. As a result, our Upstream segment's third-party gathering expense decreased and its affiliate transportation and processing expense increased, and our Gathering and Transmission segments' affiliate revenue increased. As the affiliate expense and revenue are eliminated in consolidation, the net impact is a reduction in our consolidated transportation and processing expense.

As a result of the completion of the Equitrans Midstream Merger, our operations expanded from a single operating segment to three discrete operating segments reflecting our three lines of business consisting of Upstream, Gathering and Transmission.
See Note 11 to the Consolidated Financial Statements for further discussion of the Equitrans Midstream Merger.

Commodity prices were volatile in 2025, and we expect commodity prices to continue to be volatile in 2026 due to macroeconomic uncertainty, changes to the regulatory environment and geopolitical instability and tensions, including in Venezuela, Russia, Ukraine and the Middle East, and potential further imposition of domestic and foreign tariffs. Our revenue, profitability, liquidity and financial position will continue to be impacted in the future by the market prices for natural gas and, to a lesser extent, NGLs and oil.

In response to price volatility in the natural gas market and to optimize in-basin pricing, we implement strategic curtailments from time to time to reduce our gross production. During the year ended December 31, 2025, strategic curtailments resulted in decreased sales volumes of approximately 14 Bcfe. Low natural gas prices or volatility in the natural gas market may result in adjustments to our 2026 planned development schedule and/or adjustments to the development schedule of non-operated wells in which we have a working interest. We cannot control or otherwise influence the development schedule of non-operated wells in which we have a working interest. Adjustments to our 2026 planned development schedule or the development schedule of non-operated wells in which we have a working interest, including due to declines in natural gas prices, the pace of well completions, access to sand and water to conduct drilling operations, access to sufficient pipeline takeaway capacity, unscheduled downtime at processing facilities or otherwise, could impact our future sales volume, operating revenues and expenses, per unit metrics and capital expenditures.

On July 4, 2025, President Trump signed the OBBBA into law. See Note 6 to the Consolidated Financial Statements for further discussion of the OBBBA. We expect the enactment of the OBBBA to favorably impact our projected cash income tax obligations over the next five years by deferring the payment of a significant portion of current federal income taxes.

President Trump has also executed several executive orders, some of which impact the oil and gas industry, and he and others in Congress have indicated the potential for further changes to regulations, many of which could impact the oil and gas industry, as well as the implementation of tariffs on foreign goods and services. It is uncertain at this time to what extent such changes in regulations and tariffs will impact our business. Tariffs on foreign goods and services could result in other countries instituting tariffs on U.S. goods and services, which could impact the demand for and price of natural gas, increase the price of supplies and raw materials that we rely on to conduct our business, and impact interest rates. A changing regulatory environment and domestic or foreign tariffs could ultimately impact our future sales volume, operating revenues and expenses, per unit metrics and capital expenditures.

天然氣 NGLs 與石油總計
賓夕法尼亞州 西維吉尼亞州 俄亥俄州 總計
paragraphs: 本公司為一垂直整合的天然氣公司，業務範圍包括上游、集氣與輸氣業務，主要集中在阿巴拉契亞盆地。截至2025年12月31日，本公司在約230萬英畝的土地與約2,945英里管線基礎設施上，擁有28.0十億立方英呎（Tcfe）的已證天然氣、NGLs與石油儲備。此外，本公司持有Mountain Valley Pipeline, LLC（MVP A）的A系列投資，該投資擁有Mountain Valley Pipeline（MVP Mainline），這是一條長303英里的管線，從西弗吉尼亞州的Wetzel縣延伸至維吉尼亞州的Pittsylvania縣。

本公司核心業務策略為成為天然氣領域的低成本生產者，並建立一個能在商品價格週期中產生可持續自由現金流的商業模式。此策略依賴於本公司大量的核心鑽井地點庫存、橫跨阿巴拉契亞盆地的廣泛中游基礎設施、投資等級的信用指標、低排放的運營特徵以及最佳等級的團隊與文化。作為美國唯一規模龐大的整合天然氣生產商，本公司相信我們在市場波動時期具有優勢，並能服務日益增長的需求來源，包括發電、工業消費、國內資料中心發展與液化天然氣出口。

本公司運營策略聚焦於執行大規模、多鑽井點開發專案，我們稱之為combo-development。Combo-development透過最大化運營與資本效率，在儲備開發過程的各個層面創造價值。在鑽井階段，鑽機花更多時間鑽井，較少時間轉移至新地點。先進的規劃，是執行combo-development的前提，有助於批量交付壓裂砂與管線新鮮與回收水，並提供持續滿足完井供應需求的能力，以及使用如天然氣驅動的電力壓裂等環保技術。我們的運營策略進一步因強大的中游管線與服務而增強，這些管線與服務與我們的開發計劃時程同步。我們同步的開發計劃支持一個整合的商業模式，使開發成本低落，並減少我們對未來生產進行對沖的需求。
Combo-development與較分散的開發方式相比，也提供了重要的環境與社會效益。我們的運營策略與我們的可持續性框架整合，強調持續改善排放表現、數據品質與透明度、員工培訓與利害關係人參與。透過集中開發活動，combo-development導致較少的鑽井點、減少的卡車交通、較低的燃料消耗、較短且較少的地面幹擾期間以及較少的中游建設，有助於改善安全表現與減少環境與社區影響。

此外，我們的整合商業模式使我們在不同價格環境中具有韌性。在低商品價格時期，我們的中游資產因具有類似年金的特性，能產生穩定、可預測的長期收入，支持可持續的自由現金流。在高商品價格時期，我們的低成本結構允許較低水平的財務對沖，從而增加對高天然氣價格的敞口。相應地，我們已實施強大的資本配置策略，用以負責任地開發資產並為內生增長做準備，同時透過債務償還、基本股息與機會性的股票回購，將資本回饋給股東。我們也專注於維持與強化投資等級的信用指標，這有助於我們在市場週期中獲得可靠且低成本的資金。
我們相信，透過選擇性的戰略交易，可以增強我們運營模式的優勢，因此，我們的策略也包括透過併購、出售、合資企業及類似商業交易創造價值，以及投資於與我們核心業務運營補充，甚至在某些情況下分散我們核心業務的能源相關機會。
我們的專有數位工作環境、資產基礎的規模與連續性，以及強大的中游管線網路，使我們能執行我們核心地塊位置上多十年的combo-development專案。透過嚴謹執行我們的策略，我們旨在成為股東的首選運營商，同時支持天然氣的可靠供應，以滿足國內需求與成長中的全球需求，並以促進能源安全、可負擔性與可持續發展的方式進行。
•達成銷售量2,382十億立方英呎（Bcfe），平均實現價格為每千立方英呎（Mcfe）3.19美元。
•產生 $51 億淨現金來自營運活動。
•透過債務償還與股息，達成對股東回報策略。
◦償還總計 $14 億本金之優先票據。
◦支付總計 $3.9 億股息予股東。
◦將每季基本股息提高 5% 至每股 $0.165（年化每股 $0.66）。
•總計已證實儲備量增加 1,782 億立方英尺，或成長 7%，較 2024 年為之。

paragraphs: 下列對財務狀況及營運成果之討論與分析，應與第 8 項 "財務報表與補充資料" 所包含之合併財務報表及相關附註一併閱讀。
我們 2025 年之營運成果反映本公司於 2025 年 7 月 1 日完成之 Olympus Energy Acquisition（即取得 Olympus Energy LLC、Hyperion Midstream LLC 及 Bow & Arrow Land Company LLC（合稱 Olympus Energy）所擁有之部分石油與天然氣資產及相關上游與中游資產）。
我們 2025 年之營運成果反映 Midstream Joint Venture Transaction（定義於合併財務報表附註 9）之影響，本公司於 2024 年 12 月 30 日自第三方投資人取得 35 億美元現金對價，以換取 Midstream Joint Venture 之非控制性權益。
NEPA 非經營資產處分及 NEPA 聚集系統取得

自 2024 年 5 月 31 日起，本公司營運成果反映（i）本公司於 First NEPA 非經營資產處分中處分本公司在美國東北部賓夕法尼亞州非經營天然氣資產之 40% 未分割權益，以及（ii）本公司取得 NEPA 聚集系統（定義於合併財務報表附註 11）之 100% 所有權，此為本公司於 NEPA 聚集系統取得（定義於合併財務報表附註 11）及 First NEPA 非經營資產處分中取得之額外權益所致。
此外，本公司 2025 年之營運成果反映本公司於 2024 年 12 月 31 日完成之 Second NEPA 非經營資產處分（與 First NEPA 非經營資產處分合稱 NEPA 非經營資產處分）中處分本公司在美國東北部賓夕法尼亞州非經營天然氣資產之剩餘 60% 未分割權益。有關 NEPA 非經營資產處分之進一步討論，請參閱合併財務報表附註 12。
自 2024 年 7 月 22 日起，本公司營運成果反映本公司於 Equitrans Midstream 合併（定義於合併財務報表附註 11）中取得之資產之營運。
Equitrans Midstream 合併後，先前由 Equitrans Midstream 提供本公司之聚集與輸送服務，現由本公司之上游分部透過本公司之聚集與輸送分部以關聯交易方式提供。因此，本公司上游分部之第三方聚集費用減少，其關聯運輸與處理費用增加，而本公司聚集與輸送分部之關聯收入增加。由於關聯費用與收入於合併時已抵銷，因此對本公司合併後之運輸與處理費用產生淨減額之影響。
因完成 Equitrans Midstream 合併，本公司營運從單一營運分部擴展為三個獨立營運分部，反映本公司三大業務線，包括 Upstream、Gathering 與 Transmission。
有關 Equitrans Midstream 合併之進一步討論，請參閱財務報表附註第 11 項。
2025 年商品價格波動，我們預期 2026 年商品價格仍將持續波動，因總體經濟不確定性、法規環境變動及地緣政治不穩定與緊張，包括委內瑞拉、俄羅斯、烏克蘭及中東地區，以及可能進一步實施國內外關稅。我們未來的營業收入、獲利能力、流動性及財務狀況將持續受到天然氣市場價格的影響，並在較小程度上受到 NGLs 與石油價格的影響。

為應對天然氣市場價格波動，並優化盆地內價格，我們偶爾會實施戰略性減產，以減少本公司毛利率的天然氣產量。在截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日之會計年度，戰略性減產導致銷售量減少約 14 Bcfe。天然氣價格偏低或市場波動可能導致調整本公司 2026 年預計開發計畫，以及調整我們在非經營性油井中擁有工作權益之開發計畫。我們無法控制或影響我們在非經營性油井中擁有工作權益之開發計畫。調整本公司 2026 年預計開發計畫或非經營性油井之開發計畫，包括因天然氣價格下降、油井完井速度、進行鑽井作業所需砂與水的取得、足夠輸氣管線容量的取得、處理設施未預期停機時間或其他因素，可能影響我們未來銷售量、營運收入與費用、單位指標及資本支出。
2025 年 7 月 4 日，特朗普總統簽署 OBBBA 法案成為法律。有關 OBBBA 法案之進一步討論，請參閱財務報表附註第 6 項。我們預期 OBBBA 法案的實施將有利於我們未來五年預計的現金所得稅義務，透過延後支付大部分現行聯邦所得稅。

特朗普總統亦已執行數項行政命令，其中一些影響石油與天然氣產業，且他與國會其他人士已表示可能進一步修改法規，許多法規可能影響石油與天然氣產業，以及實施對外商品與服務的關稅。目前尚無法確定這些法規變動與關稅將對本公司業務產生多大影響。對外商品與服務的關稅可能導致其他國家對美國商品與服務實施關稅，這可能影響天然氣的需求與價格，提高我們執行業務所依賴的供應品與原材料的價格，並影響利率。法規環境的變動以及國內或國際關稅，最終可能影響我們未來的銷售量、營運收入與費用、單位指標及資本支出。

headings: 與天然氣上游、中游及處理作業相關的風險
我們面臨與我們油井、管線及設施運作相關的風險。
針對我們系統或天然氣基礎設施的恐怖攻擊或武裝衝突，可能會對我們的運作造成重大不利影響。
我們的鑽探位置是分多年排程的，使其容易受到不確定因素的影響，這些因素可能會大幅改變鑽探的發生時間或時機，甚至可能完全不會鑽探。
未能及時開發我們租賃的實物財產，可能會導致資本支出增加及/或租賃的減損。
我們並未擁有我們管線及設施所在地的所有土地，這可能會干擾我們的運作及未來發展。
我們可能因租賃財產的所有權瑕疵而產生損失。
實際未來天然氣、NGLs 及石油產量的數量與時間難以預測，且可能與我們的預估有顯著差異，這可能會降低我們的獲利。
我們已證實儲備所產生的折現後未來淨現金流標準化衡量方式，與我們預估天然氣、NGLs 及石油儲備的當前市場價值不同。
適用於我們業務的財務與市場風險
我們可能無法因競爭及其他因素而提高客戶通量及相應收入，這可能會限制我們在集氣分部與輸送分部的成長能力。
財務危機或總體經濟、商業或地緣政治條件惡化，可能會對我們的營運及財務狀況造成重大不利影響。
paragraphs: 除本年度報告書第 10-K 表格所載之其他資訊外，以下風險因素使投資本公司成為一種投機性或風險性行為，應在評估本公司業務與未來展望時加以考慮。請注意，尚有其他未為本公司所知或目前認為不重要之風險，亦可能對本公司業務與營運產生負面影響。若下列所描述之任何事件或情況實際發生，將可能使本公司業務、財務狀況或營運成果受損，並導致本公司 EQT 普通股或其他證券之交易價格下跌。
天然氣之鑽探、生產、集輸、傳輸、儲存與處理為高風險且成本高昂之活動，並伴隨許多不確定性。本公司未來之財務狀況、現金流與營運成果，皆取決於營運活動之成功，而營運活動受許多超出本公司控制範圍之風險影響。
許多因素可能限制、延宕、中止或取消本公司預定之鑽探計畫、本公司未經營但持有工作權益之油井（稱為非經營油井）之開發進度，以及本公司之集輸、傳輸、儲存與處理營運，包括以下各項：
•因遵守法規要求而產生之延宕，包括因許可、廢水處理、溫室氣體排放及水力壓裂活動之限制所導致之限制；
•設備、鑽機、管線、材料、合格人力、用水（用於水力壓裂活動）或其他天然資源之短缺或取得延宕；
•供應鏈中斷或勞動力短缺之影響； •設備故障、事故或其他未預期之營運事件；
